message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on rural highways, 35 mph on urban highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if a school bus is stopped). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Stop signs: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians. | | **Headlights & Signals** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, 15 ft of a stop sign, or 30 ft of a railroad crossing.
• Parking on a shoulder is prohibited unless marked. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on a two‑lane road unless passing. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus moves again. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Only authorized towing companies may tow vehicles.
• Towing must be done with proper signage and lighting. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Registration must be renewed annually.
• Proof of insurance is required; minimum liability coverage is $30,000/60,000/25,000 (Bodily Injury/Property Damage). | | **Traffic Violations & Penalties** | • Fines vary by offense; points are added to the driver’s record.
• Accumulating 6 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension. | | **Special Rules** | • “No‑stop” lanes on highways: only for vehicles traveling at or above the posted speed limit.
• “No‑passing” zones: no overtaking in marked areas. | ### How to Stay Informed - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official rules, updates, and downloadable PDFs. - **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. - **Local County Courts** – For specific enforcement practices and local ordinances. If you need more detailed information on a particular aspect (e.g., DUI penalties, school bus rules, or recent legislative changes), let me know!
